original.target_description: Experiment 2 relationship between stimulus velocity and reaction time to colour change at a fixed central location, across three colour-change probabilities. Relationship located in narrative and Fig. 3; no main-effect F or corresponding p printed.

n.sample_role: Female observers contributing reaction times in Experiment 2; two had also taken part in Experiment 1.
n.exclusions: Results report 10 missing responses, 17 anticipations and 74 false alarms; no participant exclusion reported. Final trial count and exact exclusion rule not separately supplied for this experiment.

replication.target_description: Single unnumbered experiment: effect of stimulus velocity (0, 4.4, 17.6 degrees/s) on reaction time to coloration change; seven participants; repeated-measures ANOVA.

n.location: p. 2, Materials and methods—Participants; p. 4, Results—Reaction Times
n.quote: Seven participants (six females and one male, aged 20–25) took part in this experiment.
n.sample_role: Participants in the repeated-measures reaction-time ANOVA; seven participants described, with participant count corroborated by F(2,12).
n.exclusions: RTs over 1000 ms and below 100 ms excluded: 16 misses and 146 anticipated responses out of 2100 responses; no participant exclusion reported.

reported_success.quote: Psychophysical results replicate the findings from the previous study showing decreased RTs to coloration changes with increase of velocity of the color changing stimulus.

notes:
Known study mismatch: the 2014 paper has a single unnumbered experiment, not a distinct Experiment 2. Replication fields describe the located velocity–reaction-time test only and must not be treated as a separate Experiment 2. Authors’ success statement is an overall behavioral verdict, not an Experiment 2 verdict. Original full text unavailable after publisher 403 and repository timeout.
Source follow-up: Published article, Vision Research 46 (2006), pp. 1848–1855; title/authors/DOI match. PDF page 4 rendered and inspected. The sole printed ANOVA on this page is the interaction between uncertainty and velocity, F (4, 12) D .774, p D .562, rather than the supplied target relationship/main effect of velocity. It is not substituted for the target statistic. Target relationship is explicitly described but its own F and p are unavailable. Canonical-text quote preserves observes and line-end partici-; rendered PDF confirms those words. Canonical D elsewhere represents a rendered equals sign. Original-only target; replication and reported_success intentionally unassigned. Explicit ellipses mark interleaved column omissions in quotations.
